overview: Two reproductive strategies in animals, differing in whether the young develop inside eggs laid outside the body or inside the mother.
genZNote: Oviparous: ship the baby out in an egg to finish cooking. Viviparous: keep the oven on inside until it's fully done.

aspects.label: Where the Embryo Develops
aspects.valueA: Outside the mother's body, inside a laid egg.
aspects.valueB: Inside the mother's body, nourished directly via a placenta or similar structure.

aspects.label: Source of Nourishment
aspects.valueA: Relies on yolk stored within the egg.
aspects.valueB: Receives nourishment continuously from the mother's bloodstream.

aspects.label: Example
aspects.valueA: Birds, most reptiles, most fish, insects.

aspects.label: Typical Offspring Survival
aspects.valueA: Generally more offspring produced, but with lower individual survival rates and less parental protection during development.
aspects.valueB: Fewer offspring produced, but with higher individual survival rates due to protected internal development.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: A few animals like the platypus lay eggs (oviparous) despite being mammals — an exam-favourite exception.
overlay.memoryTrick: Ovi- = egg (oviparous lays eggs). Vivi- = alive (viviparous gives birth to live young).
overlay.commonMisconception: Not all mammals are viviparous — monotremes like the platypus and echidna are an important exception that lay eggs.
